# ADR-1073: Reading a transcript has one implementation and refuses a non-path

## Status

accepted

## Context

ADR-1072 added `infrastructure/transcript_activity.py` and left two loose ends the review of PR #592 named.

`scanner.iter_tool_uses` (ADR-0595) streamed the same thing: every assistant `tool_use` block of a transcript, whole file, line by line. Nothing in the repository called it, in any layer, in any script or benchmark; `git log -S` finds it arriving in the bulk commit `dc6876c9` and never referenced since. It also carried the two defects the three review rounds of PR #592 closed in the new module: `rec.get("type")` on a record that may not be an object, and `(rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")` on a `message` that may be a truthy non-object.

`transcript_activity` itself raised `TypeError` at `Path(transcript_path)` for a truthy argument that is neither text nor a path. Its signature says `str | Path | None`, but the value reaches it from the SessionEnd event's JSON envelope, where nothing is typed, and it runs in a hook path with no `try`/`except` around it: the same class of crash as the two already fixed, one field further out.

## Decision

`scanner.iter_tool_uses` is deleted. A transcript is read in one place, `transcript_activity`, which returns the ordered tool sequence and the turn count; a future caller that needs the tool inputs or line numbers extends that function rather than reviving a second reader.

`transcript_activity` returns the empty result for a `transcript_path` that is not a `str` or an `os.PathLike`, exactly as it does for a missing file, instead of raising.

## Consequences

Easier: one reader to fix when the transcript format moves, and no call into the hook path can raise on an ill-typed argument.

`tests_py/infrastructure/test_transcript_activity.py` covers a number, a float, a bool, a list and a dict as the path, and a `Path` object still working. The type cases raise `TypeError` on the previous code.

Harder: nothing measured. The deleted generator yielded `{"name", "input", "line"}` per tool call, which `transcript_activity` does not; ADR-0595 keeps the record of what it was, and the git history keeps the code.
